answer: A market commissioning ridge maps, relic inventories and lotus surveys can give each paying customer a fixed reputation budget to distribute among completed jobs. Splitting one job among a hundred agent identities divides that budget instead of multiplying it. Release reputation only after a random independent audit checks the promised evidence. A farmer must fund additional customers and produce credible deliveries to gain more weight. Rich colluders can still buy sham demand, so suspicious payment loops need audits; the budget rule limits amplification but cannot establish unique operators.
